subproblem.title: Derivative of the mollified set integral: D(∫_G ρ(· − z)dz)(x)w = ∫_G Dρ(x − z)w dz (parent Step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let G ⊆ ℝ^N be Lebesgue null-measurable, and let ρ : ℝ^N → ℝ be C¹ with compact support. Put u(x) := ∫_G ρ(x − z) dL^N(z). Then for all x, w ∈ ℝ^N, Du(x)w = ∫_G Dρ(x − z)w dL^N(z). Here Du(x) = fderiv ℝ u x is Lean's total Fréchet derivative (which is 0 at points of non-differentiability) and Dρ(t) = fderiv ℝ ρ t. (The proof shows that u is in fact differentiable at every x, with Du(x) = ∫_G Dρ(x − z) dz.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (G : Set (Rn N)) (ρ : Rn N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet G volume → ContDiff ℝ 1 ρ → HasCompactSupport ρ → ∀ x w : Rn N, fderiv ℝ (fun x ↦ ∫ z in G, ρ (x - z)) x w = ∫ z in G, fderiv ℝ ρ (x - z) w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 1 ("u is C¹; Du(x)k = ∫_G Dρ(x − z)k dz", by differentiation under the integral sign). This is the differentiability of the mollified function u_σ = φ_σ ⋆ ũ used throughout Simon Ch. 2, §2 (mollification paragraph and Lemma 2.5, chapter-02.txt lines 530-596), with χ_G in place of u and a general C¹ kernel ρ in place of φ_σ. Here the differentiation under the integral sign is carried out directly for the measure λ := L^N⌞G (Lebesgue measure restricted to G), which avoids the change of variables to the convolution ρ ⋆ χ_G. Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm, B_s(a) and B̄_s(a) the open and closed balls, Dv(t) = fderiv ℝ v t.

1. (Bounds on ρ and Dρ.) Since ρ is C¹, it is differentiable everywhere and Dρ : ℝ^N → L(ℝ^N, ℝ) is continuous (ContDiff.differentiable, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, both with 1 ≠ 0). The derivative vanishes off the topological support of ρ (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport), so Dρ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). Being continuous with compact support, Dρ is bounded: there is C with ‖Dρ(t)‖ ≤ C for all t (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Since tsupport ρ is compact, it is bounded, so there is R with tsupport ρ ⊆ B̄_R(0).

2. (Translates and reflections.) For each fixed a ∈ ℝ^N the map z ↦ a − z is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N (Homeomorph.subLeft a), so z ↦ ρ(a − z) and z ↦ Dρ(a − z) are continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). Hence they are L^N-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport) and therefore integrable on G, i.e. λ-integrable (Integrable.integrableOn). Continuous functions are strongly measurable, so they are a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure, in particular for λ.

3. (Pointwise derivative of the integrand.) For fixed z, the map x ↦ ρ(x − z) is ρ composed with x ↦ x − z, whose derivative is the identity (HasFDerivAt.sub_const); by the chain rule it has derivative Dρ(x − z) at every x.

4. (Domination.) Fix x₀ ∈ ℝ^N and let s := B_1(x₀), a neighbourhood of x₀. Define b(z) := C if z ∈ B̄_{R+1}(x₀) and b(z) := 0 otherwise. Claim: ‖Dρ(x − z)‖ ≤ b(z) for all z ∈ ℝ^N and all x ∈ s. If z ∈ B̄_{R+1}(x₀) this is step 1. If z ∉ B̄_{R+1}(x₀), then x − z ∉ tsupport ρ: otherwise |x − z| ≤ R, and |z − x₀| ≤ |z − x| + |x − x₀| < R + 1 (as |x − x₀| < 1), contradicting z ∉ B̄_{R+1}(x₀); hence Dρ(x − z) = 0 (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport) and the claim holds. The function b is C times the indicator of the compact set B̄_{R+1}(x₀), which has finite Lebesgue measure, so b is L^N-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const) and hence λ-integrable.

5. (Differentiation under the integral sign.) Apply the dominated differentiation theorem (Mathlib hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le) with the measure λ, the neighbourhood s, F(x, z) := ρ(x − z), F'(x, z) := Dρ(x − z) and the bound b. Its hypotheses hold by steps 2-4: F(x, ·) is a.e.-strongly measurable for every x; F(x₀, ·) is λ-integrable; F'(x₀, ·) is a.e.-strongly measurable; ‖F'(x, z)‖ ≤ b(z) for every z and every x ∈ s; b is λ-integrable; and for every z and every x ∈ s, x ↦ F(x, z) has derivative F'(x, z) at x. Therefore u(x) = ∫ F(x, z) dλ(z) has at x₀ the derivative L := ∫_G Dρ(x₀ − z) dz, a Bochner integral in the Banach space L(ℝ^N, ℝ); thus Du(x₀) = L (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

6. (Evaluation at w.) Evaluation at w is a continuous linear map L(ℝ^N, ℝ) → ℝ, and z ↦ Dρ(x₀ − z) is λ-integrable by step 2, so evaluation commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply): Du(x₀)w = (∫_G Dρ(x₀ − z) dz)w = ∫_G Dρ(x₀ − z)w dz. Since x₀ and w were arbitrary, this proves the claim. ∎

Remark. The null-measurability of G is not used: λ = L^N⌞G is a measure for every set G. The hypothesis is kept so that the convolution route of the parent proof (integral_indicator₀ plus HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left) remains available.

subproblem.title: Fubini swap for the mollified weight against μ: ∫ζ(y)(∫ρ(y − z)dμ(z))dy = ∫(∫ζ(y)ρ(y − z)dy)dμ(z), with integrability
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on ℝ^N (Borel σ-algebra), let ζ, ρ : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous with compact support, let r ∈ ℝ with tsupport ρ ⊆ B̄_r(0), and suppose μ(K') < ∞ for K' := cthickening(r, tsupport ζ), the closed r-neighbourhood of tsupport ζ. Then the function y ↦ ζ(y)∫ρ(y − z) dμ(z) is L^N-integrable, and ∫ ζ(y)(∫ ρ(y − z) dμ(z)) dL^N(y) = ∫ (∫ ζ(y)ρ(y − z) dL^N(y)) dμ(z). All integrals are Bochner integrals, so the integral of a non-integrable function is 0. For y ∉ tsupport ζ the factor ζ(y) vanishes, so the integrand ζ(y)∫ρ(y − z)dμ(z) is 0 there whether or not z ↦ ρ(y − z) is μ-integrable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ζ ρ : Rn N → ℝ) (r : ℝ), Continuous ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → Continuous ρ → HasCompactSupport ρ → tsupport ρ ⊆ Metric.closedBall (0 : Rn N) r → μ (Metric.cthickening r (tsupport ζ)) < ∞ → Integrable (fun y ↦ ζ y * (∫ z, ρ (y - z) ∂μ)) ∧ ∫ y, ζ y * (∫ z, ρ (y - z) ∂μ) = ∫ z, (∫ y, ζ y * ρ (y - z)) ∂μ

Source: the last step of the implementation note of the parent proof ("Tonelli's theorem for the non-negative continuous integrand (y, z) ↦ ζ(y)ρ(y − z), which vanishes unless (y, z) ∈ T × K' and may therefore be integrated against the finite measures L^N restricted to T and μ restricted to K'"), together with Step 0 of the parent proof (ζ̃(z) := ∫ζ(y)ρ(y − z)dy vanishes off K'). In the proof of Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 543-596), this is the step that turns the pointwise bound into the integrated bound by a mollified test function. No sign conditions are needed here: Fubini's theorem for integrable functions is used instead of Tonelli. Since μ is not assumed s-finite, Fubini is applied to the finite measure μ' := μ⌞K'. Notation: T := tsupport ζ (compact) and F(y, z) := ζ(y)ρ(y − z). Lean's Bochner integral is 0 for non-integrable functions; the manipulations in steps 5-6 (pulling out a constant factor, restricting to a set off which the integrand vanishes) hold without any integrability.

1. (Vanishing.) Let y, z ∈ ℝ^N with F(y, z) ≠ 0. Then ζ(y) ≠ 0, so y ∈ T. Also ρ(y − z) ≠ 0, so y − z ∈ tsupport ρ ⊆ B̄_r(0), i.e. dist(z, y) = |y − z| ≤ r. Hence z ∈ cthickening(r, T) = K' (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Contrapositively, F(y, z) = 0 whenever z ∉ K', and also whenever y ∉ T.

2. (The finite measure μ'.) μ' := μ⌞K' satisfies μ'(ℝ^N) = μ(K') < ∞, so μ' is a finite, hence s-finite, measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). Lebesgue measure L^N on ℝ^N is σ-finite.

3. (Integrability of F on the product.) F is continuous on ℝ^N × ℝ^N, as the product of ζ ∘ pr₁ and ρ ∘ (pr₁ − pr₂), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for L^N ⊗ μ'. Continuous functions with compact support are bounded, say |ζ| ≤ M_ζ and |ρ| ≤ M_ρ; then |F| ≤ M_ζ M_ρ everywhere. By step 1 the support of F lies in T × ℝ^N. That set has (L^N ⊗ μ')-measure L^N(T)·μ'(ℝ^N) < ∞ (Measure.prod_prod; T is compact, so L^N(T) < ∞). A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function is integrable on a set of finite measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). As the support of F is contained in T × ℝ^N, F is L^N ⊗ μ'-integrable (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).

4. (Fubini.) By step 3, Fubini's theorem (integral_integral_swap) gives ∫(∫ F(y, z) dμ'(z)) dL^N(y) = ∫(∫ F(y, z) dL^N(y)) dμ'(z). Moreover y ↦ ∫ F(y, z) dμ'(z) is L^N-integrable (Integrable.integral_prod_left).

5. (Inner integrals.) For each y, F(y, ·) vanishes off K' by step 1. So ∫ F(y, z) dμ'(z) = ∫_{K'} F(y, z) dμ(z) = ∫ F(y, z) dμ(z) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). This equals ζ(y)∫ρ(y − z) dμ(z) (constant factor; integral_const_mul).

6. (Outer integral.) For z ∉ K', F(·, z) ≡ 0 by step 1, so H(z) := ∫ F(y, z) dL^N(y) = 0. Hence ∫ H dμ' = ∫_{K'} H dμ = ∫ H dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).

This is the pointwise form of the identity ∫ g·∇u_σ = −∫ u div(φ_σ ⋆ g) in the proof of Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 543-596), tested against the single field ρ(y − ·)w. Since B̄_r(y) is closed, tsupport φ = closure(support φ) ⊆ B̄_r(y) (closure_minimal). Equivalently, if z ∉ B̄_r(y) then |y − z| > r, so y − z ∉ tsupport ρ.

2. (Derivative of φ.) The map z ↦ y − z has derivative −id (HasFDerivAt.const_sub). Since ρ is C¹ it is differentiable, and by the chain rule φ has derivative Dφ(z) = Dρ(y − z) ∘ (−id) = −Dρ(y − z) at every z (HasFDerivAt.comp, then HasFDerivAt.congr_fderiv).

3. (The test field.) Let h(z) := φ(z)w ∈ ℝ^N. Then h is C¹, being the C¹ scalar function ρ ∘ (y − ·) times a constant vector (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.smul). Its topological support satisfies tsupport h ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_r(y) ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left and step 1). And h has compact support, because tsupport h is a closed subset of the compact ball B̄_r(y) (ℝ^N is proper; IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).

4. (Divergence of the test field.) By step 2 and the product rule for a scalar function times a constant vector (HasFDerivAt.smul_const), Dh(z) is the rank-one map k ↦ (Dφ(z)k)w = −(Dρ(y − z)k)w, i.e. Dh(z) = (−Dρ(y − z)).smulRight w. Alternatively, with an orthonormal basis (e_i), Σ_i ⟨e_i, ℓ(e_i)w⟩ = ℓ(Σ_i ⟨e_i, w⟩e_i) = ℓ(w). Hence div h(z) = −Dρ(y − z)w for every z.

5. (Gauss–Green.) By step 3, h is admissible in the Gauss–Green identity of the pair, so ∫_{G∩U} div h dL^N = −∫ ⟨h(z), ν(z)⟩ dμ(z). 2. (μ-integrability of φ.) φ is continuous (ρ composed with z ↦ y − z), so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ. Since ρ is continuous with compact support it is bounded, |ρ| ≤ M for some M (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), so |φ| ≤ M. If φ(z) ≠ 0 then y − z ∈ tsupport ρ ⊆ B̄_r(0), so |z − y| ≤ r; thus support φ ⊆ B̄_r(y). A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function is integrable on a set of finite measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), so φ is μ-integrable on B̄_r(y). Since its support lies in B̄_r(y), φ is μ-integrable (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset). Put A := ∫ φ dμ; then A ≥ 0 because ρ ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg).

3. (Reduction to directional bounds.) By the operator-norm criterion (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound, applicable as A ≥ 0) it suffices to show |Du(y)w| ≤ A|w| for every w ∈ ℝ^N.

4. (Representation.) Fix w. Apply the sibling lemma fderiv_setintegral with x = y; its hypotheses (G null-measurable, ρ C¹ with compact support) are hypotheses here. It gives Du(y)w = ∫_G Dρ(y − z)w dz. Apply the sibling lemma kernel_gauss_green to U, G, μ, ν, ρ, r, y, w; its hypotheses (U open, IsGaussGreenPair U G μ ν, ρ C¹ with compact support, tsupport ρ ⊆ B̄_r(0), B̄_r(y) ⊆ U) are all hypotheses here. It gives ∫_G Dρ(y − z)w dz = ∫ ρ(y − z)⟨w, ν(z)⟩ dμ(z). Hence Du(y)w = ∫ φ(z)⟨w, ν(z)⟩ dμ(z).

5. (Estimate.) For μ-a.e. z, |ν(z)| = 1 (hGG.2.2.2.1). Then, as ρ ≥ 0, the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality (abs_real_inner_le_norm) gives |φ(z)⟨w, ν(z)⟩| = φ(z)|⟨w, ν(z)⟩| ≤ φ(z)|w||ν(z)| = φ(z)|w|. The majorant z ↦ φ(z)|w| is μ-integrable by step 2 (Integrable.mul_const). The estimate |∫ F dμ| ≤ ∫ g dμ for an integrable a.e. majorant g of |F| holds without assuming F integrable (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). Therefore |Du(y)w| = |∫ φ(z)⟨w, ν(z)⟩ dμ(z)| ≤ ∫ φ(z)|w| dμ(z) = A|w| (integral_mul_const).

6. By steps 3 and 5, ‖Du(y)‖ ≤ A = ∫ ρ(y − z) dμ(z). ∎

Remark. The case r < 0 is included: then B̄_r(y) = ∅, ρ ≡ 0, and steps 1-6 apply verbatim.
